explanations.text:
import the line differ, json, the pattern matcher, the shell, and
[the map run](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py) and [the tool](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py)

CROSS_RE
the look of a pin into another map: the name, a colon, e and the entry number, a colon, the anchor words.
the name is a file's path or a human file's name. the form is the same. only the reading of the name changes.

SYNC_PROMPT
the letter to claude when the project changed: read the changed files, mend the words the change made wrong, add a sentence for a behaviour the reader would ask about, keep every pin, and give an entry of the user's own words the smallest edit in the user's voice


the project's own human file json is an abstraction of the whole codebase. another human file json is an abstraction of multiple files or folders.
both have no code of its own.
both have pins which reach: 
  other files,
  one block of a file
  one anchor of a file's abstraction
  another human file abstraction

[cmd_map_project](cmd_map_project)(abstraction_name)
    the abstraction name is what you typed after human map <name>: the text on stdin, --verbatim when
    the words are yours, and no --block, because the project map has no blocks of its own.
    The tool checks every pin, refuses a circle, and appends one entry. It prints how
    many pins reach files, entries of other maps, and earlier entries of this map — and
    how many files of the project have a pin.
    With --verbatim the words must come in plain — a pin is refused, because the pins
    come after, with retext — and a copy stays beside the entry as the origin.

[build_anchors](build_anchors)(abstraction_text, data, self_id, root)
    abstraction text is the abstraction being mapped.
    data is the map it goes into; self_id is the entry's own number.
    The tool walks the pins of the text one by one. A pin whose target reads like
    app/main.py:e1:the start is [a pin into another map](cross_anchor);
    every other pin — a file, a block of a file, an earlier abstraction of this map — goes to
    [the shared pin checker](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:build_anchors) one at a time.
    Two pins with the same words are refused here, because the shared checker sees
    only one pin at a time.

[cross_anchor](cross_anchor)(words, name, eid, aw, project_root)
    name is what the pin points at; 
    eid is the entry number; 
    aw is the anchor words.
    call [name_to_map(name, project_root)](compiler/cli/human/helpers.py:name_to_map) and get the map path and its sort type.
    if name sort type file. then it must be a file of the project.
    if name sort type human file. there's no file to check.
    
    the tool refuses the pin when:
      the name has no map
      the map has no such abstraction
      when the abstraction has no anchor with those words.

    a good pin is stored with the name, the abstraction, and the anchor words, so the reader can walk from this abstraction to that abstraction, and to the anchors inside it.

[cmd_retext](cmd_retext)(a)
    a is the entry number, the new text, and --verbatim when the words are yours.
    The tool replaces the text of one project entry the way it does for a file: the pins
    other project entries point at must survive, and no circle may appear.
    The words are the text without its pins. When the words changed, the project entries
    that point into this one are marked stale; a retext that only moves the pins says so
    and marks nobody. An entry that holds your own words refuses a change of those words;
    --verbatim lets the change through and keeps the new text as the origin, or puts the
    flag on an entry that had none. A stale mark the new text did not answer stays, and
    the tool names the repair.

[cmd_undo](cmd_undo)(a)
    a is the entry number, or nothing for the last project entry.
    The tool removes that entry — unless another project entry points into it.

[cmd_show](cmd_show)(a)
    The tool prints every project entry with its pin count, a stale mark that names every
    file's entry and every earlier entry that changed, and, for an entry of your own words,
    that it holds them — and whether they were reworded since they were mapped, with the
    way to bring them back among the warnings. Then the other warnings: a pin whose file is
    gone, whose block is gone, whose entry or anchor in another map is gone
    ([the cross check](check_cross)), whose stored lines are old. Last,
    [the coverage](print_coverage): the files of the project that have a pin, out of all of
    them, and the names of the files without one.


the two doors the file maps knock on

[pins_into](pins_into)(root, code_name, eid)
    The anchor words of entry eid of the file code_name that the project map points at.
    A retext, a sync, or a stale repair of that entry adds these to
    the words it must keep, and an undo of that entry is refused while the set is not
    empty. Empty when there is no project map.

[mark_stale](mark_stale)(root, code_name, eid, old_text)
    The tool adds a note to every project entry that points into entry eid of code_name —
    the file, the entry, and the old text — and gives back their numbers. The file's
    retext, sync, and stale repair call it after the words changed, so the project telling
    knows a fact under it moved. The note joins the ones the entry already holds, one per
    parent; a parent already noted keeps its first old text, so a second change does not
    hide the first.


the project changed

[cmd_sync](cmd_sync)(a)
  The old state of the project is git HEAD, so --old is refused. With --stale the tool
  goes to [the stale repair](repair_stale) instead. --for names the entry the change
  was written for; it must exist, and it is refused together with --stale.

    ●  the tool asks git what moved                        ([the files that changed](changed_files))
    │     The files the project knows — listed or pinned — that git sees
    │     changed, added, or gone, against HEAD.
    │
    ●  the tool takes a second look at every pin           ([the second look](re_resolve))
    │     File pins, block pins, and pins into other maps; a gone target
    │     is broken and is reported by its name. The candidates are the entries that pin a changed
    │     file, plus the entries with a broken pin. The entry named by
    │     --for leaves the candidates unless one of its pins is broken:
    │     its pins follow the code, its words stay. With no candidate the
    │     map is saved — no claude call.
    │



cli writes the request to ai compiler
the request has:
  the root, 
  the changed files with their full paths, 
  [the diff of the files a candidate pins](project_diff):
    if no git, the diff of the lines its pins reach,
  [the broken pins](broken_note), each with the anchors its abstraction holds now, so a reworded anchor can be retargeted
  the files of the project, 
  the candidate texts, each named as the user's words when it holds them
  the words other abstractions need.



    ●  claude answers, the tool checks                     ([the asking](ask))
    │     Up to --tries times. Each answer is [rebuilt on a copy](rebuild) and
    │     refused when a pin is dead, a needed anchor is gone, or an entry
    │     that is not a candidate was rewritten; the refusal goes back to
    │     claude with its name.
    │
  the map is saved
          The changed texts are reported line by line, with a warning for
          every entry of your own words the answer changed. The entries that
          point into a changed one are marked stale — when the words changed,
          not when the pins alone moved.

[repair_stale](repair_stale)(a, root, data, name)
    ●  the tool gathers every parent the notes name
    │     An entry of a file's map when a note names a file, an earlier
    │     project entry otherwise. A parent that is gone stops the run.
    │
    ●  the tool writes the second letter
    │     The shared stale letter of [the file repair](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:repair_stale),
    │     one page per parent — its old text, its new text, the diff between
    │     them, and the form a pin at it takes: file, entry, and anchor words
    │     when the parent lives in a file; entry and anchor words otherwise.
    │     An entry of your own words adds one rule: the smallest edit, in
    │     your voice.
    │
    ●  claude answers, the tool checks
    │     The answer must keep the words other entries need and make no
    │     circle, up to --tries times.
    │
    ●  the map is saved
          The mended text replaces the old one, every note goes, and the
          project entries that point into this one are marked stale in turn —
          when the words changed. A repair that moved your own words is
          named on the spot.


# HELPER FUNCTIONS

[root_of](root_of)()                        
the project root, climbing from where you stand

[map_path](map_path)(root, name)            
the map of the name: a file's map or a human file's json

[load](load)(root, name)                    
the map of the name, or an empty one

[save](save)(root, data, name)              
writes the map of the name

[files_of](files_of)(root)                  
the file list of human/human.json

[map_of](map_of)(root, fname)
the map of one name, a file or a human file or nothing when it has none.

[entry_of](entry_of)(data, eid)             
one entry of a map by its number

[counts](counts)(anchors)                   
the pin count line: into files, into other maps, into earlier entries

[check_cross](check_cross)(x, root)         
why a pin into another map is dead, or nothing when it holds

[git](git)(root, *args)                     
runs git at the root and gives back its exit code and output

[old_text_of](old_text_of)(root, rel)       
the file as git HEAD holds it, empty for a new file

[changed_files](changed_files)(root, data)  
the files the project knows — listed or pinned — that git sees changed, added, or gone

[project_diff](project_diff)(root, changed) 
one unified diff over the changed files a candidate pins, HEAD against the disk
if no git, the diff of the lines its pins reach

[re_resolve](re_resolve)(data, root, name)  
the shared second look, plus a check of every pin into another map

[broken_note](broken_note)(broken, root)    
the broken pins for the letter, each with the anchors its entry holds now

[rebuild](rebuild)(trial, texts, cand, root) 
puts the answered texts into a copy of the map and checks every pin and every needed word

[ask](ask)(prompt, root, tries, check)      
claude up to tries times, with the refusal sent back each time

[cmd_lines](cmd_lines)(a)                   
refused: the project has no lines of its own

[print_coverage](print_coverage)(root, data) 
files with a pin out of all files, and the ones without

anchors.words: the diff of the files a candidate pins
